rationale: Genesis 26:34-35 reports that Esau married 'Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite' and that 'they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah' (BSB). Rebekah takes this up at 27:46: 'I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?' In this app's BSB, 'Hittite women' occurs only at Genesis 27:46 and 1 Kings 11:1 (script scan), and 'these' points back to wives already named. At 28:1 Isaac sends Jacob away with 'Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women', and at 28:8-9 Esau, 'seeing that his father Isaac disapproved of the Canaanite women', marries Mahalath, Ishmael's daughter. The Cambridge Bible on 26:35 cross-references 'Genesis 27:46, Genesis 28:8', and Ellicott on 26:34 writes that 'the place of these two verses would rightly be at the beginning of Genesis 27'. Graded explicit_reference because Rebekah refers to the same women. It is strong rather than explicit, following conn-gen19-lot-deuteronomy2, because 27:46 names neither wife. The range runs to 28:9 because the frame closes there, with Esau's third marriage. Genesis 36:2-3 lists Esau's wives with different names and fathers; that difference is reported in the lesson, not resolved here.
